t: You're looking at the Wellcome Library, a free library and research collection open to the public. It grew from the collection of Sir Henry Wellcome, who founded it. His interest was the history of medicine in a broad sense, and the shelves reach into alchemy, witchcraft, anthropology and ethnography too. Wellcome made his money in pharmaceuticals, and when he died in 1936 he left capital for charitable work, which became the Wellcome Trust. The Trust now looks after the collection and pays for new acquisitions. The building was designed by Septimus Warwick, an architect who began by designing town halls.
